raw_response:
I will keep most of my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the most stable income for me, and I still keep a smaller piece in cotton. I have only 10.1 mu and only 2 people in the house, with some off-farm work, so I cannot spread myself too thin. This year I’ll put about 7.1 mu in wheat-maize and 3.0 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize are my backbone. Cotton can make money, but it takes more labor, especially later for management and picking, so I won’t make cotton too big.

For fertilizer, I do not like cutting too much. The extension guy talks about balanced fertilization, and I listen some, but after farming this long I still trust what I saw on my own land. If wheat looks weak, I lose yield quickly, so I would rather keep a steady rate and split it. Maize I plant right after wheat harvest, so the turnaround is tight and I keep tillage simple. Cotton I manage a bit more carefully but not too heavily, because labor and cash both matter. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages, but not waste pumping money if rainfall is decent.
